proof_attempt_summary: Derived matched original-record minimax risk, finite globally honest connected-interval length and worst-null adaptation orders for bounded heterogeneous potential tables with exactly sparse degree-two realized means, and generalized to every K>=4 and arbitrary preregistered profile pairs. Mathematical and rubric panels passed with no findings, both cited sources were attested, and independent terminal validity confirmed a subfield ceiling below the fixed field floor (projected score 7 < 7.4). The logarithmic elbow is credited to prior work; favorable complete-factorial geometry, conservative often-uninformative interval constants and absent practical-gain evidence limit publication tier; no Lean/F stage was launched.
tldr: For every balanced full factorial experiment with integer \(K\ge4\) and any preregistered distinct profile pair at distance \(h\), the original-record minimax squared risk has order \(t^2\log(1+D_h/t^2)/N\), where \(D_h=h(K-h+1)\) and \(t=\min(s,D_h)\). Globally finite \(0.90\)-honest connected intervals and their worst expected length over zero-mean tables have the square-root order. Total observable thresholding and clipping attain these bounds without support recovery or a variance floor. Full-class honesty prevents uninflated sparsity adaptation whenever the larger-to-smaller frontier ratio diverges. The Gaussian logarithmic elbow is fully credited; its validity here is proved for heterogeneous bounded fixed tables and all original records.
gap: Selection-consistent factorial inference does not give weak-signal finite minimax precision; independent sequence-model results do not cover this assignment experiment.
